definition: Beating softened butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, incorporating air for a tender crumb.
Working cold fat into flour with fingertips until sandy -- no air incorporated, unlike creaming.
Pricking a rolled dough (like shortbread) with a fork before baking to let steam escape evenly.
The ingredient (baking soda, baking powder, whipped egg whites) responsible for a cookie's rise.
Carefully heating and cooling chocolate so it sets glossy with a clean snap.
Milk and sugar cooked slowly until caramelized into a thick, spreadable caramel -- central to alfajores.
High-cocoa-butter chocolate formulated for dipping and tempering rather than baking into dough.
French for 'sandy' -- both the crumbly texture and the name of the cookie built around it.
